# Customer Sentiment

`customer_support.obj.core.customer_sentiment` · v1.0.0 · **draft** · scope **core**

> How the customer currently feels about us, inferred from behaviour and language rather than asked. It is a read, not a fact: it has a confidence, a provenance and a decay, and it is never the same thing as a survey answer. The load-bearing field is `trajectory`, not `polarity` — where the feeling is going matters more to every downstream decision than where it currently sits, because the actions available differ completely. A frustrated customer on a recovering trajectory needs us to keep doing exactly what we are doing; a satisfied customer on a collapsed one needs a phone call today. Read only from the customer's own words and their own behaviour, never from ours.


Also called: `Sentiment`, `Customer Mood`, `Tone Read`, `Emotional State`

## Constraints

- **`cs.sent.not_a_survey_answer`** Sentiment may never be reported as, or written from, a satisfaction score. One is inferred during and one is stated after, and the disagreement between them is the only calibration this object has.
- **`cs.sent.our_text_cannot_measure_them`** A read whose sample includes our own messages may not be published as customer sentiment. This is a correctness constraint, not a quality one.
- **`cs.sent.never_customer_visible`** An inferred sentiment label is never a customer-visible field and never appears in outbound copy. Telling a customer the system has classified them as hostile is the fastest available way to make it true.
- **`cs.sent.no_agent_performance_scoring`** Sentiment must not be attributed to an individual agent as a performance metric. Well-run queues route the angriest customers to the strongest agents, so the metric inverts and punishes exactly the behaviour it should reward.
- **`cs.sent.one_message_is_not_a_read`** A single message produces a mood, not a sentiment. Reads below the minimum sample must be reported as unreadable rather than neutral.
- **`cs.sent.compare_within_locale_only`** Reads may be compared within a language and locale and not across one. Politeness norms differ systematically and always in the same direction, so cross-locale aggregates rank the most reserved cultures as the happiest customers. _(soft)_
- **`cs.sent.incident_correlation_is_not_relationship`** During a declared major incident, sentiment across the affected base moves together and carries no information about any individual relationship. Account-level flags raised in that window must be re-evaluated after resolution, not carried forward. _(soft)_


## Business rules

- **`cs.sent.trajectory_must_accompany_polarity`** A sentiment read published without a trajectory is incomplete and must not be routed to a de-escalation decision. Negative-and-recovering and negative-and-deteriorating require opposite actions, and a bare polarity cannot distinguish them.

- **`cs.sent.our_text_is_not_their_sentiment`** A read whose measured_on is our_text must be discarded, not down-weighted. It is a measurement of our own tone and it improves whenever agents write more apologetically.

- **`cs.sent.never_substitute_a_survey_answer`** A Satisfaction Score must never be written into polarity and polarity must never be reported as a satisfaction result. One is inferred during, the other is stated after; the gap between them is this object's only honest calibration signal and merging them destroys it.

- **`cs.sent.silence_is_not_neutral`** When we owe the reply and the customer has been silent for days, polarity must not be reported as neutral. Absence of complaint is not presence of contentment, and the customer who stops chasing has usually stopped expecting.

- **`cs.sent.broken_commitment_overrides_language`** While a commitment to this customer is past due, the trajectory must be read as deteriorating regardless of how pleasant the last message was. What we did outranks what they wrote.

- **`cs.sent.hostile_needs_behavioural_corroboration`** A hostile classification derived from language alone, with no behavioural corroboration (silence, repeat contact, channel switch, audience widening), is advisory only and must not by itself route a customer to an escalation queue. Rule 11 — only independent evidence raises confidence.

- **`cs.sent.apology_does_not_close_uncertainty`** When about_uncertainty is true, a reply containing no specific next update time must not be recorded as having addressed the sentiment. It addressed the etiquette.

- **`cs.sent.read_expires_at_next_inbound`** A read taken before the customer's most recent message is stale and must be treated as absent rather than carried forward. Stale sentiment is worse than none because it looks current.

## Outputs

- **`polarity_read`** Current level, with its provenance attached. Never emitted without trajectory_read. → L4.reasoning_unit
- **`trajectory_read`** Direction and window. The half of the read that decides which action is even available. → L4.reasoning_unit, L4.decision_maker
- **`read_confidence_bp`** Confidence in the read itself, not the negativity of it. Drops to zero when measured_on is our_text. → L4.reasoning_unit
- **`de_escalation_required`** True only when a negative level meets a non-recovering trajectory and behavioural corroboration. → L4.decision_maker
- **`tone_directive`** How to write to this person right now — length, formality, whether to apologise again. Read by Layer 5.2, never by Layer 4. → L5.2.channel_planner
- **`update_deadline_hours`** When the next substantive update must land to hold the recovery window open. The output Layer 5 can actually schedule. → L5.execution_planning, L5.communication_planning
- **`churn_precursor`** Collapsed trajectory regardless of polarity. The quiet ones. → L4.reasoning_unit
- **`survey_suppression`** Do not send a satisfaction survey into an unresolved hostile thread. → L5.communication_planning
- **`inferred_vs_stated_delta`** Difference between what this object inferred and what the survey later said. The only thing that calibrates every pattern above. → L6.learning_unit

## Actions

- **Give a specific next update** (human) — Name a time and a person. Uncertainty-driven anger responds to a timestamp and does not respond to sympathy; this is the highest-yield and lowest-cost move in the whole domain.
- **Stop apologising and change the substance** (human) — The third apology without new information reads as stalling and is what converts frustrated into hostile. An apology is a one-time instrument.
- **Call instead of writing** (human) — Voice collapses hostility faster than any written sequence, and it also removes the paper trail the customer was building — which is a reason it is sometimes refused, and that refusal is itself a signal.
- **Check in on a disengaged customer** (human) — One short, non-transactional message. The only available response to dangerous_calm, and the reason that pattern is allowed to be uncertain — the action is cheap enough to be wrong about.
- **Hand to a named owner** (human) — A change of person, not a change of queue. Hostility aimed at an individual rarely recovers with that individual still on the thread, and routing without renaming the owner achieves nothing.
- **Suppress the satisfaction survey** (system) — Do not survey an unresolved hostile thread. It collects a score we already knew and spends the single ask we had on this relationship.
- **Re-read after the next customer message** (system) — Never re-read after our own reply. Reading sentiment immediately after we write measures our tone and reliably shows improvement we did not cause.
- **Record inferred read against the later survey answer** (system) — The only mechanism by which any confidence in this file becomes evidence-based rather than argued. Cheap, boring, and almost never built.


## Evidence

- **survey** · 8500 bp — A written verbatim is the customer's own account of how they felt. The strongest thing we can get — and it is late, self-selected and about a moment that has already passed.
- **call_recording** · 8000 bp — Voice carries what edited text conceals. Expensive to obtain, almost never available at the moment the read is needed.
- **ticket** · 7000 bp — Reopens, repeat contact, channel switches. Behaviour rather than language, and behaviour cannot be polite.
- **email** · 6000 bp — Written tone. Real evidence, and the single most easily faked in both directions — by them out of courtesy, by us out of anxiety.
- **chat** · 5500 bp — Closer to speech than email and therefore less edited. Short turns make any per-message classifier unreliable.
- **derived** · 4500 bp — Engine-computed observation balance. Corroborating only, and capped here specifically because it cannot yet separate our words from theirs.
- **telemetry** · 4000 bp — Usage collapse alongside an open thread. Circumstantial, lagging, and the only witness the silent customer leaves.
- **status_page** · 2500 bp — Explains attribution, never polarity. Useful for deciding what the feeling is about and useless for deciding how strong it is.


## Metrics

- **read_accuracy** (percent) — Share of inferred reads later agreed with by the survey answer that arrived. Calibrates every pattern in this file and is the only honest score this object has.
- **recovery_rate** (percent) — Share of negative reads that became non-negative inside the recovery window. The number that actually measures de-escalation, and almost nobody has it because almost nobody stores a trajectory.
- **silent_negative_share** (percent) — Share of negative reads that never produced a complaint. The entire reason this object exists rather than a complaints queue.
- **false_hostile_rate** (percent) — Hostile classifications a human reviewer overturned. Watched harder than accuracy: a false hostile routes a calm customer into an escalation path and manufactures the sentiment it claimed to find.
- **read_coverage** (percent) — Share of live conversations carrying any read at all. Rises for the wrong reason if unreadable messages are scored neutral, so it is only meaningful next to unreadable_share.
- **time_to_first_negative_read** (hours) — How long after the first customer message the read turns. Shorter is better and it measures the pipeline, not the customer.
- **contaminated_read_share** (percent) — Reads with measured_on of our_text or mixed. Today this is effectively all of them, and stating it as a metric keeps that fact visible instead of embarrassing.


## Examples

- **Furious on Monday, terse and cooperative on Thursday** — polarity frustrated, trajectory recovering. The correct action is to change nothing and keep the update cadence exactly as it is. Most systems escalate here, introduce a new person, and undo three days of work.
- **Unfailingly polite, replies within minutes, renewal in six weeks, has stopped asking when it will be fixed** — The most dangerous record in the queue and the one no language model flags. polarity satisfied, trajectory collapsed, expression_style terse. Nothing in the words is wrong.
- **Profane in every message for two years** — baseline_temperament abrasive. This is a baseline, not a signal. Flagging it hostile every week is how a team learns to ignore the field entirely.
- **"No problem, take your time" — for the third time this month** — repeat_frustration true, attributed_to wait_time, about_uncertainty true. The words say patient; the frequency says exhausted. Per-message scoring reads this as the happiest thread in the queue.
- **Angry about a twenty-minute outage that is already fixed** — Real anger with no remaining cause. attributed_to product_defect, recovery_window_hours short. Closing the ticket closes the sentiment; treating it as a churn signal spends an escalation on nothing.
- **Read computed over our own three-paragraph apology** — measured_on our_text. Discard, do not down-weight. It is a measurement of us, and it will show sentiment improving every time an agent writes at length.
- **Formal, complete sentences and a numbered list, from someone who wrote in lowercase fragments last week** — expression_style formal_escalating. Politeness went UP and risk went up with it. The clearest textual escalation warning there is, and most models score the change as an improvement.

## Metadata

owner **Customer Support** · updated 2026-08-08 · review **unreviewed** · confidence **provisional** · completeness **partial**


> Ten of eighteen patterns are executable today, which makes this the strongest day-one object in the Customer Support brain by a wide margin — derived.sentiment, derived.engagement, thread.ball_in_court, commitment.due_at, meeting.start_at and the reply_cadence baseline are all real, and between them they carry a genuine read.
The eight needs_signal entries are ranked in the order they should be built. First derived.sentiment_by_author, because it is a correctness fix rather than a feature: every executable confidence in this file is capped several hundred basis points below where it could sit purely because the engine cannot yet separate the customer's words from ours. Second derived.sentiment_trend, because a level cannot express a trajectory and trajectory is what this object is for. Everything after those two is additive.
The uncomfortable admission this file makes deliberately rather than hides: two of the executable patterns (pushback_at_the_answer, audience_widening_on_our_ball) sit at or below 5000 and are authored as corroboration only. They are here because they are honestly what the substrate offers, not because they are good, and pushback_at_the_answer should be deleted outright the day a support-native dissatisfaction observation kind ships.
